name: CursorPanCamera
src_typeComment: Plug-and-play top-down/isometric camera panning, two independent styles in one component: - Edge Pan (MOBA/RTS-style, e.g. League of Legends' default camera): move the cursor to the edge of the screen and the camera pans in that direction, continuously, for as long as it stays there. - Drag Pan (mobile-map / MOBA middle-mouse style, e.g. Google Maps or League's Alt+drag): hold a mouse button and drag — the camera moves in the OPPOSITE direction of the cursor's movement, like you're grabbing and dragging the world itself rather than steering the camera directly. Both are plain toggles (enableEdgePan / enableDragPan) so you can run either alone or both together — while a drag is active it takes priority over edge-panning, so the two never fight each other in the same frame.

src_serialized.name: enableEdgePan
src_serialized.tooltip: Move the cursor to the edge of the screen to pan the camera in that direction.

src_serialized.name: edgeThickness
src_serialized.tooltip: How close to the screen edge (in pixels) the cursor must be before edge-panning kicks in.

src_serialized.name: requireCursorInWindow
src_serialized.tooltip: If true, edge-panning stops while the cursor has left the game window entirely (e.g. dragged onto a second monitor) — without this, the camera would keep panning forever since the cursor can never move back into a window it isn't in.

src_serialized.name: enableDragPan
src_serialized.tooltip: Hold dragButton and move the mouse to pan the camera in the OPPOSITE direction of the mouse movement, like dragging a map.

src_serialized.name: dragButton
src_serialized.tooltip: 0 = Left click, 1 = Right click, 2 = Middle click.

src_serialized.name: panOnGroundPlaneXZ
src_serialized.tooltip: Pans along the world XZ (ground) plane — the usual choice for a top-down/isometric camera. Turn off for a 2D/side-scrolling camera, which pans along its own local XY plane instead.

src_members.sig: public Vector2 ComputeEdgePanDirection(Vector2 mousePosition, float screenWidth, float screenHeight)
src_members.name: ComputeEdgePanDirection
src_members.comment: Public, pure logic (no Input/Screen dependency) — which edge(s) the cursor is touching, given a screen position and dimensions. Update() just feeds it the real Input.mousePosition/Screen.width/ Screen.height every frame.

src_members.sig: public Vector2 ComputeDragPanDelta(Vector2 currentMousePosition, Vector2 previousPosition)
src_members.name: ComputeDragPanDelta
src_members.comment: Public, pure logic — the actual "opposite direction" math. Dragging the cursor RIGHT should move the camera/world LEFT (as if you grabbed a point on the ground and are pulling it toward you), hence the negation.

src_members.name: ToWorldOffset
src_members.comment: Projects a 2D pan amount onto whichever plane this camera actually moves along.
